title: Modality Alignment across Trees on Heterogeneous Hyperbolic Manifolds
claim: Prior methods align one flat visual feature with hierarchical text asymmetrically; ours builds hierarchies for both modalities and aligns them symmetrically.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right, balance-scale icon under each alignment panel
description: The figure has two horizontally stacked rows separated by a dashed line. The top row is labeled 'Previous Methods' and the bottom row 'Our Method'. In each row a bird photo goes through a peach trapezoid labeled Visual encoder. The output feeds a white box with feature trees. In the top row, a single visual feature is shown next to a hierarchical textual tree under the heading 'Euclidean'. A tilted balance scale below it is captioned 'asymmetric alignment on Euclidean spaces'. In the bottom row, a blue hyperbolic cone holds the visual tree and a pink cone holds the textual tree, and a level scale is captioned 'symmetric alignment on hyperbolic manifolds'. A Textual encoder takes taxonomy labels (Aves, Bucerotiformes, Aceros) running from coarse to fine. At the right, prediction panels show heatmapped bird images. Top: red crosses and one check, labeled 'inferior prediction'. Bottom: green checks, labeled 'optimal prediction'. Red bold text marks the key terms.
caption: Comparison between previous methods and our method. Previous methods extract a single visual feature to align with hierarchical textual features in Euclidean spaces. This asymmetric alignment leads to inferior prediction. In contrast, our method achieves a symmetric alignment by extracting hierarchical visual features on hyperbolic manifolds, leading to optimal prediction.
abstract: Modality alignment is critical for vision-language models (VLMs) to effectively integrate information across modalities. However, existing methods extract hierarchical features from text while representing each image with a single feature, leading to asymmetric and suboptimal alignment. To address this, we propose Alignment across Trees, a method that constructs and aligns tree-like hierarchical features for both image and text modalities. Specifically, we introduce a semantic-aware visual feature extraction framework that applies a cross-attention mechanism to visual class tokens from intermediate Transformer layers, guided by textual cues to extract visual features with coarse-to-fine semantics. We then embed the feature trees of the two modalities into hyperbolic manifolds with distinct curvatures to effectively model their hierarchical structures. To align across the heterogeneous hyperbolic manifolds with different curvatures, we formulate a KL distance measure between distributions on heterogeneous manifolds, and learn an intermediate manifold for manifold alignment by minimizing the distance. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the optimal intermediate manifold. Experiments on taxonomic open-set classification tasks across multiple image datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms strong baselines under few-shot and cross-domain settings.
